correctness.rationale: The claim is finite and algorithmically exhaustive: for each n<=6 encode all 2^binom(n,2) labelled graphs, test connectivity with BFS, compute each G-v exact integer characteristic polynomial and rational greatest-root isolation, compare roots using disjoint rational intervals or gcd-common-root certification, then quotient exceptions by all n! relabelings. Inspected actual checker.py has explicit loops and aborts on unresolved overlapping intervals; witnesses have characteristic polynomials giving spectral radii 2 versus sqrt(2+sqrt2), and a cubic maximum-degree root versus sqrt((5+sqrt17)/2). An independently written separate enumerator examined all 26,704 connected n=6 graphs and recovered connected totals 1,4,38,728,26704; arbitrary-degree failures 0,0,0,150,7740; all-max-degree failures 0,0,0,0,540; n=6 class sizes {180,360}. Independent second check used floating point and therefore corroborates but does not replace the repository exact root-isolation certificate. The smallest opposing eigenvalue gap was >0.031 in independent numerics.
residual_risks: Spectral proxy is not empirical patch survival or extinction; no probabilistic ecological model.

final_claim: For connected simple unweighted graphs through six vertices, every maximum-degree deletion minimizes post-loss spectral radius through n=4; at n=5 degree tie-breaking first fails in three isomorphism classes, but some maximum-degree deletion remains optimal; at n=6 exactly two isomorphism classes (180 and 360 labelled realizations) defeat every maximum-degree choice.
limitations: Enumerated only connected simple graphs n=2..6 and one vertex deletion, not larger graphs or weighted/directed networks.
